p01.why: The header shared-limit.h is not in the batch directory, so the specification cannot settle this; my guess is that it defines one_limit as an inline const variable (one object), each_limit as a plain const variable (one per unit), and declares far_limit extern, so every check passes.

p02.why: The inline static member is one object defined in the class in both units, so count becomes 5 and the addresses match.

p03.why: inline is not allowed on a non-static data member.

p04.why: An inline function that no code uses needs no definition.

p05.why: An inline variable and an inline function work in one unit, and next returns 2.

p06.why: inline is not allowed on a block-scope function declaration.

p07.why: S is not complete inside its own class body, so an inline static member of type S is not valid.

p08.why: inline on a declaration after the definition: GCC accepts, and Clang and EDG reject.

p09.why: The static local of the inline function is one object for both units, so the third call returns 3.

p10.why: The implicit special members are inline, so both units can have them, and the sum is 2.

p11.why: An inline function is defined twice in one unit.

p12.why: A virtual function can be inline.

p13.why: inline is not allowed on a class definition.

p14.why: A namespace-scope constexpr variable is not inline, so each unit has its own object and the addresses differ.

p15.why: A plain declaration after the deleted definition gives no second definition; the specification does not say this directly, so this is my reading.

p16.why: A member function defined in its class is inline, so both units can define it.

p17.why: f is inline in only one unit, which needs no diagnostic; the evidence says the program links and runs at -O0.

p19.why: A friend function defined in its class is inline and found for a call with an S argument, returning 4.

p20.why: A used inline function has no definition; EDG rejects during translation, and Clang and GCC fail at link time.

p21.why: Each unit has its own internal-linkage local, so the sum is 2 plus 3.

p22.why: A static member declared in the class can be defined inline outside it.

p23.why: The two inline definitions differ, which needs no diagnostic, and the program accepts either body.

p24.why: The const static member is defined inline outside the class with 9.

p25.why: The inline variable is used without a definition, and the evidence says all three compilers report it during translation.

p26.why: inline is not allowed on a parameter.

p27.why: A friend declaration can be inline without being a definition.

p28.why: inline is not allowed on a type alias.

p29.why: count is not inline and is used, but it has no definition outside the class.

p30.why: inline is not allowed on a block-scope variable.

p31.why: A function can be declared inline before its definition; there is no main.

p32.why: A constexpr function is inline, so both units can define it, and 9 plus 9 is 18.

p33.why: An inline const variable at namespace scope has external linkage, so both units see one object.

p34.why: A static constexpr member is inline, so it is one object for the program.

p35.why: inline is not allowed on a block-scope variable, even a static one.
